dedupe_keys.name: r5py rapid realistic routing on multimodal transport networks in python

description: r5py is a Python library that wraps the Conveyal R5 routing engine to compute travel time matrices and accessibility on multimodal networks, covering walking, cycling, public transport and car trips. It takes a street network from OpenStreetMap, public transport timetables in GTFS and origin and destination points held as GeoPandas tables, and returns travel times and accessibility indicators as data frames. The developers, including Christoph Fink, Willem Klumpenhouwer, Marcus Saraiva, Rafael Pereira and Henrikki Tenkanen, publish it on GitHub with documentation at r5py.readthedocs.io and a Zenodo citation. It is free and dual licensed under GPL-3.0-or-later or MIT at the user's choice. The releases page read on 2026-09-29 lists v1.1.7 of 29 June 2024 as the latest, so it counts as inactive under the two-year rule, although releases were frequent through 2024. Coverage is any place with input data and it was not run. Caveats: a Java runtime is needed by R5 and results depend on feed quality. It suits accessibility and network flow studies of public transport. Related catalogue records: model-opentripplanner and model-openrouteservice.
